source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies multilayer sample selection and derives sharp analytic within-firm causal-mean bounds using response-type restrictions; its stated target is not a cross-world harmed-stayer ratio.
Theorem 2 gives the sharp identified interval for the fraction negatively affected from factual treatment-arm outcome margins via Fréchet--Hoeffding coupling.
The paper characterizes ordinary-bootstrap consistency for directionally differentiable maps and develops an alternative derivative-estimation resampling route.
The numerical-delta method uses an appropriately shrinking finite-difference step to provide consistent inference for directionally differentiable functions.
The paper proposes bootstrap-calibrated projection confidence intervals for smooth functions/components of partially identified parameter vectors, with uniform asymptotic coverage.
The preprint studies aggregated conditional linear-program values, represents support-function boundaries as averages of regression-function intersections, and gives regular asymptotic theory.
